edges.source: PLG Missense Variant with Preserved Plasminogen Secretion

edges.description: Proposed, unproven link: reduced fibrinolytic reserve may allow venous thrombi to persist, probably only with additional thrombotic risk factors.
Proposed link from impaired fibrinolysis to cerebral infarction, based on pedigrees and selected case series without controls.
The orthologous substitution reproduces the loss of plasmin catalytic activity.
edges.limitations: Homozygous mice only; most human carriers are heterozygous.

edges.description: Plasma from the knock-in mice shows slower fibrin clot lysis.
edges.limitations: Clot lysis was measured in vitro in plasma; acute experimental thrombosis models in one genetic background did not reveal an in vivo thrombotic consequence.

nodes.description: There is no disease-specific treatment, and no therapy is indicated for asymptomatic carriers. Thrombotic events in carriers have been managed with standard anticoagulation such as warfarin; duration has been decided case by case.

evidence.reference_title: A case of acute pulmonary embolism associated with dysplasminogenemia.
evidence.snippet: Life-long anticoagulation therapy was initiated. He is currently under follow-up without clinical events for 2 yr.

evidence.reference_title: [Thrombotic complication in the course of aplastic anemia-paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria syndrome; possible involvement of dysplasminogenemia (plasminogen Tochigi) in the pathogenesis of thrombosis].
evidence.snippet: He was given warfarin for the prevention of thrombosis in December 1994. As of October 1995, these was no recurrence of thrombosis.

nodes.description: Cerebral infarction has been reported in young heterozygous p.Ala620Thr carriers in Chinese pedigrees and in a selected series of 18 patients with infarction and low plasminogen activity. A Japanese case-control comparison found no excess of plasminogen deficiency in cardioembolic stroke.

evidence.reference_title: Analysis of cerebral infarction caused by dysplasminogenemia in three pedigrees.
evidence.snippet: In this report we describe three notable cases of cerebral infarction (CI) complicated with dysplasminogenemia in young patients.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-Phenotype Correlation of Hereditary Plasminogen Deficiency: Molecular Mechanisms From 18 Patients With Cerebral Infarction.
evidence.snippet: The 18 patients' cranial magnetic resonance (MRI) revealed recent cerebral infarct lesions in all cases. PLG:A levels ranged from 19% to 67%. All patients were diagnosed with dysplasminogenemia.

evidence.reference_title: Population-based distribution of plasminogen activity and estimated prevalence and relevance to thrombotic diseases of plasminogen deficiency in the Japanese: the Suita Study.
evidence.snippet: The incidence of plasminogen deficiency in an age- and sex-matched control group (13/324, 4.01% for deep vein thrombosis or 13/330, 3.94% for stroke) selected from the 4517 individuals was not significantly different from those in patients with deep vein thrombosis (3/108, 2.78%) or cardioembolic stroke (6/110, 5.55%).

nodes.description: Venous thrombosis has been reported in individual carriers, starting with the index Tochigi patient, but controlled family and population studies find no increased risk, and many reported patients had other thrombotic risk factors. The association is disputed.

evidence.reference_title: Abnormal plasminogen. A hereditary molecular abnormality found in a patient with recurrent thrombosis.
evidence.snippet: A patient who suffered a recurring thrombosis over the last 15 yr has been investigated. The only abnormality found in this patient was a significantly depressed level of plasminogen activity in plasma.

evidence.reference_title: A case of acute pulmonary embolism associated with dysplasminogenemia.
evidence.snippet: He was diagnosed as PE with deep vein thrombosis without apparent risk factors.

evidence.reference_title: The prevalence and clinical manifestation of hereditary thrombophilia in Korean patients with unprovoked venous thromboembolisms.
evidence.snippet: The most common types of HT was AT III deficiency (14 of 222, 6.3%) and PC deficiency (12, 5.4%), followed by PS deficiency (4, 1.8%), and dysplasminogenemia (3, 1.4%) (Fig 1).

evidence.reference_title: Population-based distribution of plasminogen activity and estimated prevalence and relevance to thrombotic diseases of plasminogen deficiency in the Japanese: the Suita Study.
evidence.snippet: Among 19 patients with homozygous plasminogen deficiency showing about 10% plasminogen activity, none had deep vein thrombosis.

evidence.reference_title: Population-based distribution of plasminogen activity and estimated prevalence and relevance to thrombotic diseases of plasminogen deficiency in the Japanese: the Suita Study.
evidence.snippet: These findings indicate that neither heterozygous nor homozygous plasminogen deficiency constitutes a significant risk factor for thrombotic disease.

evidence.reference_title: Severe dysplasminogenemia due to homozygous PLG Ala620Thr variant in a Korean woman without a history of venous thromboembolism: A case report and literature review.
evidence.snippet: We believe that this clinically silent homozygous case supports the previous findings that isolated PLG Ala620Thr variant does not confer a significant risk of VTE.

nodes.description: The variant plasminogen is cleaved by plasminogen activators into two-chain plasmin, but the plasmin is catalytically inactive or impaired. For p.Ala620Thr the substituted threonine lies next to the catalytic histidine and is proposed to block the proton transfer of the serine-protease mechanism. In heterozygotes, half of the circulating molecules are defective, so specific activity is about half normal.

animal_models.description: The orthologous substitution reproduces the loss of plasmin catalytic activity.
animal_models.name: Plg-Tochigi knock-in mouse (Plg p.Ala622Thr homozygous)

evidence.reference_title: Plasminogen Tochigi: inactive plasmin resulting from replacement of alanine-600 by threonine in the active site.
evidence.snippet: The Thr at position 55 in plasminogen (plasmin) Tochigi may perturb His-57 such that the proton transfers associated with the normal catalytic process cannot occur in the abnormal plasmin.

evidence.reference_title: [Thrombotic complication in the course of aplastic anemia-paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria syndrome; possible involvement of dysplasminogenemia (plasminogen Tochigi) in the pathogenesis of thrombosis].
evidence.snippet: Abnormal PLG is converted by urokinase to an inactive two-chain plasmin molecule.

evidence.reference_title: Novel compound heterozygous mutations in plasminogen (p.Gly568Arg/p.Ala620Thr) impair protein structure and function in type II deficiency: mechanistic insights into a hereditary thrombogenic disorder.
evidence.snippet: p.Ala620Thr destabilized the catalytic triad (His603-Asp646-Ser741)

meta.association: Germline missense variant (heterozygous, homozygous or compound heterozygous)

evidence.reference_title: Plasminogen Tochigi: inactive plasmin resulting from replacement of alanine-600 by threonine in the active site.
evidence.snippet: Amino acid sequence analysis of a tryptic peptide isolated from the abnormal plasminogen indicated that Ala-600 (equivalent to Ala-55 in the chymotrypsin numbering system) had been replaced by Thr.

evidence.reference_title: Severe dysplasminogenemia due to homozygous PLG Ala620Thr variant in a Korean woman without a history of venous thromboembolism: A case report and literature review.
evidence.snippet: The missense variant PLG Ala620Thr is the major cause of dysplasminogenemia in East Asian countries, including Korea.

nodes.description: Germline PLG missense variants, most often in the serine-protease domain (p.Ala620Thr near the catalytic histidine; also p.Gly568Arg, p.Gly712Arg, p.Gly751Arg and others), leave PLG transcription, plasminogen synthesis and secretion intact, so circulating plasminogen antigen stays normal while the protein is functionally defective.

evidence.reference_title: Novel compound heterozygous mutations in plasminogen (p.Gly568Arg/p.Ala620Thr) impair protein structure and function in type II deficiency: mechanistic insights into a hereditary thrombogenic disorder.
evidence.snippet: In vitro functional assays, including RT-qPCR, ELISA, and WB analysis, confirmed that neither mutation significantly altered the expression level of mRNA

evidence.reference_title: Abnormal plasminogen. A hereditary molecular abnormality found in a patient with recurrent thrombosis.
evidence.snippet: In spite of the depressed plasminogen activity, the patient was found to have a normal level of plasminogen antigen concentration.

nodes.description: Knock-in mice homozygous for Plg p.Ala622Thr, the equivalent of human p.Ala620Thr, have about 8% of wild-type plasmin activity after urokinase activation and slower plasma clot lysis, but grow normally and show wild-type outcomes in experimental deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, focal brain ischaemia and skin wound healing.
Pulmonary embolism has been reported in isolated carriers; the association carries the same uncertainty as deep venous thrombosis.

evidence.reference_title: A case of acute pulmonary embolism associated with dysplasminogenemia.
evidence.snippet: Here we report an extraordinary case of PE complicated with dysplasminogenemia, a rare genetic disorder resulting in hypercoagulability, in a young male.

nodes.description: Reduced effective plasmin slows the proteolytic dissolution of fibrin clots in plasma. In most carriers this reduced fibrinolytic reserve has no clinical consequence; whether it contributes to thrombosis when combined with other risk factors is unresolved.

animal_models.description: Plasma from the knock-in mice shows slower fibrin clot lysis.
animal_models.name: Plg-Tochigi knock-in mouse (Plg p.Ala622Thr homozygous)

evidence.reference_title: Plasminogen Tochigi mice exhibit phenotypes similar to wild-type mice under experimental thrombotic conditions.
evidence.snippet: In vitro fibrin clot lysis in plasma was significantly slower in PlgT/T mice than in wild-type mice.

nodes.description: The defining laboratory finding: plasma plasminogen activity is reduced (about 50-70% in heterozygotes, and much lower in homozygotes and compound heterozygotes) while plasminogen antigen is normal, giving a low activity-to-antigen ratio. It is congenital and lifelong.

evidence.reference_title: The Unravelling of the Genetic Architecture of Plasminogen Deficiency and its Relation to Thrombotic Disease.
evidence.snippet: In contrast, type II is characterized by decreased plasminogen activity but normal antigen levels

evidence.reference_title: Severe dysplasminogenemia due to homozygous PLG Ala620Thr variant in a Korean woman without a history of venous thromboembolism: A case report and literature review.
evidence.snippet: His 53-year-old mother, who had no reported history of VTE, was homozygous for the PLG Ala620Thr variant with decreased plasminogen activity of just 25%.

evidence.reference_title: Analysis of cerebral infarction caused by dysplasminogenemia in three pedigrees.
evidence.snippet: PLG activity (PLG:A) in proband 1 and 3 of his tested family members, proband 2 and 2 of his tested family members, and proband 3 and her father were all reduced to roughly 50% of normal levels.

nodes.description: NM_000301 c.1858G>A, p.Ala620Thr (mature numbering p.Ala601Thr; plasminogen Tochigi; rs121918027) in exon 15, beside the catalytic histidine. Activated to two-chain plasmin with severely impaired proteolytic activity.

evidence.reference_title: Plasminogen Tochigi mice exhibit phenotypes similar to wild-type mice under experimental thrombotic conditions.
evidence.snippet: A race-specific A620T mutation in Plg, also known as Plg-Tochigi, originally identified in a patient with recurrent venous thromboembolism, causes dysplasminogenemia with reduced plasmin activity.

evidence.reference_title: Analysis of cerebral infarction caused by dysplasminogenemia in three pedigrees.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing led to the identification of a heterozygous c.1858G>A missense mutation in exon 15 of the PLG gene in these three patients and affected family members.

nodes.description: c.1702G>A, p.Gly568Arg in exon 14, reported in trans with p.Ala620Thr in a patient with cerebral infarction, 27% activity and 103% antigen; it impaired catalytic activity of recombinant plasminogen without affecting secretion.

evidence.reference_title: Novel compound heterozygous mutations in plasminogen (p.Gly568Arg/p.Ala620Thr) impair protein structure and function in type II deficiency: mechanistic insights into a hereditary thrombogenic disorder.
evidence.snippet: Sanger sequencing identified compound heterozygous missense mutations in the PLG gene: c.1702G > A (p.Gly568Arg) in exon 14 and c.1858G > A (p.Ala620Thr) in exon 15.

nodes.description: c.2108G>A, p.Gly703Asp in the serine-protease domain, found in the same cerebral-infarction series; functional consequence not characterized.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-Phenotype Correlation of Hereditary Plasminogen Deficiency: Molecular Mechanisms From 18 Patients With Cerebral Infarction.
evidence.snippet: Genetic analysis identified four types of PLG gene variants: c.1858G > A (p.Ala620Thr), c.398A > G(p.His133Arg), c.2108G > A(p.Gly703Asp), and c.1702G > A (p.Gly568Arg).

nodes.description: p.Gly712Arg (mature numbering G693R), described in the heterozygous state in type II plasminogen deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: The Unravelling of the Genetic Architecture of Plasminogen Deficiency and its Relation to Thrombotic Disease.
evidence.snippet: In addition, the missense variation p.Gly712Arg (G693R, old nomenclature) has been described in heterozygous state related to type II plasminogen deficiency

nodes.description: Plasminogen Kanagawa-I, reported as G732R in mature-protein numbering (p.Gly751Arg in precursor numbering), found in exon 18 in a healthy heterozygote with half-normal activity and normal antigen.

evidence.reference_title: Plasminogen Kanagawa-I, a novel missense mutation, is caused by the amino acid substitution G732R.
evidence.snippet: Nucleotide sequencing revealed a heterozygous G to A transition in exon 18, which resulted in an amino acid substitution of G732R.

nodes.description: c.398A>G, p.His133Arg, newly identified in a retrospective Chinese series of patients with cerebral infarction and low plasminogen activity; functional consequence not characterized.

evidence.reference_title: Genotype-Phenotype Correlation of Hereditary Plasminogen Deficiency: Molecular Mechanisms From 18 Patients With Cerebral Infarction.
evidence.snippet: Genetic analysis identified four types of PLG gene variants: c.1858G > A (p.Ala620Thr), c.398A > G(p.His133Arg), c.2108G > A(p.Gly703Asp), and c.1702G > A (p.Gly568Arg).
